subject: Automotive & EVs
title: When Will Gas Cars Disappear?
description: A short lesson to help you apply When Will Gas Cars Disappear?.

hook.text: Norway plans to ban the sale of new gas cars by 2025—dozens of countries have set targets between 2030 and 2040.

buildup.text: But banning new sales does not remove existing gas cars—those will keep driving for 15 to 20 more years.

discovery.text: Even with aggressive bans, the last gasoline car on Earth probably won't stop running until after 2060.

twist.text: Developing countries will lag further—they inherit used gas cars from wealthier nations and lack charging networks.

climax.text: The transition will be gradual and uneven—a rich country's EV future arrives decades before a poor country's.

punchline.text: Gas cars won't vanish overnight—they'll fade out over a generation.

quiz.question: Why won't gasoline cars disappear immediately after sales bans?
options: Existing gas cars will keep running for 15-20 more years

details.summary: Multiple countries have announced bans on new gasoline car sales between 2025 and 2040, but the existing fleet will take decades to cycle out of service entirely.
details.whyItMatters: Even after new gas car sales end, over a billion existing combustion vehicles will remain on roads for 10 to 20 more years, shaping emissions trajectories for decades.
takeaways: Norway aims to end new gas car sales by 2025
The EU targets 2035 for a new combustion car ban
Full fleet turnover could take until the 2050s or beyond

faq.question: Will it be illegal to drive a gasoline car after the ban date?
faq.answer: No. The bans target the sale of new combustion vehicles, not the use of existing ones. People can continue driving their gasoline cars after the ban takes effect.

faq.question: Can developing countries afford to ban gas cars on the same timeline?
faq.answer: Most developing nations lack the charging infrastructure and affordable EV options needed for rapid transition. Their timelines will likely lag by one to two decades behind wealthy countries.
